1	// Package review — see env.go for package-level rationale.
2	//
3	// tui_model.go provides reviewTUIModel, the Bubble Tea Model for the
4	// review dashboard. The model renders a per-agent status table
5	// during the run and supports Ctrl+O drill-in mode for inspecting one agent's
6	// live event buffer on the alt screen.
7	package review
8	
9	import (
10		"context"
11		"fmt"
12		"strconv"
13		"strings"
14		"sync"
15		"time"
16	
17		"charm.land/bubbles/v2/spinner"
18		"charm.land/bubbles/v2/viewport"
19		tea "charm.land/bubbletea/v2"
20		"charm.land/lipgloss/v2"
21	
22		reviewtypes "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/review/types"
23		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/stringutil"
24	)
25	
26	// agentRow holds per-agent live state during the TUI run.
27	type agentRow struct {
28		name     string
29		status   reviewtypes.AgentStatus
30		runStart time.Time          // stamped on first event from this agent
31		runEnd   time.Time          // stamped on Finished/RunError event
32		tokens   reviewtypes.Tokens // cumulative
33		preview  string             // latest AssistantText preview, capped by display width
34		buffer   []reviewtypes.Event
35		err      error
36	}
37	
38	// agentEventMsg is sent to the Bubble Tea program when an agent emits an event.
39	type agentEventMsg struct {
40		agent string
41		ev    reviewtypes.Event
42	}
43	
44	// runFinishedMsg is sent when the orchestrator calls RunFinished.
45	type runFinishedMsg struct {
46		summary reviewtypes.RunSummary
47	}
48	
49	// tickMsg triggers spinner and duration column updates.
50	type tickMsg time.Time
51	
52	// reviewTUIModel is the Bubble Tea model for the review dashboard.
53	type reviewTUIModel struct {
54		rows       []agentRow
55		rowIdx     map[string]int // agent name → row index (O(1) lookup)
56		detailMode bool
57		detailIdx  int // which agent is shown in drill-in
58		// detail is the pager backing the drill-in body. Width/Height are kept
59		// in sync with termWidth/termHeight (minus header+footer). Scroll
60		// position is internal state; AtBottom drives auto-tail.
61		detail viewport.Model
62	
63		cancel     context.CancelFunc
64		cancelOnce *sync.Once
65	
66		spinner    spinner.Model
67		termWidth  int
68		termHeight int
69	
70		finished bool
71		summary  reviewtypes.RunSummary
72	
73		// cancelling tracks whether a Ctrl+C-initiated cancellation is in flight.
74		// Set true on the first Ctrl+C (in tandem with cancelOnce firing the shared
75		// CancelFunc); the dashboard switches to a "cancelling" indicator and the
76		// footer offers a force-quit hint. A second Ctrl+C while cancelling=true
77		// force-quits without waiting for agents to drain.
78		cancelling bool
79	}
80	
81	// newReviewTUIModel builds an initial model pre-populated with one row per
82	// agent. cancel is the shared CancelFunc; it must be the same one passed to
83	// NewTUISink.
84	func newReviewTUIModel(agents []string, cancel context.CancelFunc) reviewTUIModel {
85		sp := spinner.New()
86		sp.Spinner = spinner.Dot
87		sp.Style = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(lipgloss.Color("8"))
88	
89		rows := make([]agentRow, len(agents))
90		rowIdx := make(map[string]int, len(agents))
91		for i, name := range agents {
92			rows[i] = agentRow{
93				name:   name,
94				status: reviewtypes.AgentStatusUnknown,
95			}
96			rowIdx[name] = i
97		}
98		// Seed viewport with defaults that match termWidth/termHeight so an
99		// immediate Ctrl+O before any WindowSizeMsg still renders.
100		const (
101			defaultTermWidth  = 80
102			defaultTermHeight = 24
103		)
104		vp := viewport.New(
105			viewport.WithWidth(defaultTermWidth),
106			viewport.WithHeight(defaultTermHeight-2),
107		)
108		return reviewTUIModel{
109			rows:       rows,
110			rowIdx:     rowIdx,
111			detail:     vp,
112			cancel:     cancel,
113			cancelOnce: &sync.Once{},
114			spinner:    sp,
115			termWidth:  defaultTermWidth,
116			termHeight: defaultTermHeight,
117		}
118	}
119	
120	// tickCmd schedules the next tick for duration/spinner refresh.
121	func tickCmd() tea.Cmd {
122		return tea.Tick(100*time.Millisecond, func(t time.Time) tea.Msg {
123			return tickMsg(t)
124		})
125	}
126	
127	// Init returns the initial spinner tick command.
128	func (m reviewTUIModel) Init() tea.Cmd {
129		return tea.Batch(m.spinner.Tick, tickCmd())
130	}
131	
132	// Update handles all incoming messages.
133	func (m reviewTUIModel) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
134		switch msg := msg.(type) {
135		case agentEventMsg:
136			return m.handleAgentEvent(msg)
137	
138		case runFinishedMsg:
139			m.finished = true
140			m.summary = msg.summary
141			// Sync each row's status from the orchestrator's summary. The
142			// in-stream events (Finished / RunError) update status as they
143			// arrive, but the orchestrator's classifyStatus has access to
144			// process-level signals (Wait error, ctx cancellation) that the
145			// event stream never surfaces. Without this sync, an agent that
146			// the orchestrator classified Cancelled (Ctrl+C path, no Finished
147			// emitted) or Failed (process exit non-zero, no Finished emitted)
148			// would still render as "running" in the final frame.
149			//
150			// Preserve any already-set status from the event stream — if the
151			// stream said Failed (RunError), the summary may say Succeeded
152			// (process exit 0); RunError stickiness wins. Only overwrite when
153			// the row is still in AgentStatusUnknown.
154			now := time.Now()
155			for i, run := range msg.summary.AgentRuns {
156				if i >= len(m.rows) {
157					break
158				}
159				if m.rows[i].status == reviewtypes.AgentStatusUnknown {
160					m.rows[i].status = run.Status
161				}
162				if m.rows[i].runEnd.IsZero() && !m.rows[i].runStart.IsZero() {
163					m.rows[i].runEnd = now
164				}
165			}
166			return m, nil
167	
168		case tickMsg:
169			var spinCmd tea.Cmd
170			m.spinner, spinCmd = m.spinner.Update(msg)
171			return m, tea.Batch(spinCmd, tickCmd())
172	
173		case spinner.TickMsg:
174			var spinCmd tea.Cmd
175			m.spinner, spinCmd = m.spinner.Update(msg)
176			return m, spinCmd
177	
178		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
179			m.termWidth = msg.Width
180			m.termHeight = msg.Height
181			m.detail.SetWidth(m.detailViewportWidth())
182			m.detail.SetHeight(m.detailViewportHeight())
183			m = m.refreshDetailContent()
184			return m, nil
185	
186		case tea.KeyPressMsg:
187			return m.handleKey(msg)
188		}
189		return m, nil
190	}
191	
192	// detailViewportWidth returns the viewport's width, mirroring termWidth.
193	func (m reviewTUIModel) detailViewportWidth() int {
194		if m.termWidth < 1 {
195			return 1
196		}
197		return m.termWidth
198	}
199	
200	// detailViewportHeight returns the viewport's body height, reserving one line
201	// for the header and one for the footer.
202	func (m reviewTUIModel) detailViewportHeight() int {
203		h := m.termHeight - 2
204		if h < 1 {
205			return 1
206		}
207		return h
208	}
209	
210	// refreshDetailContent re-renders the focused agent's events into the
211	// viewport. It preserves auto-tail: if the viewport was sitting at the bottom
212	// (or has no scrollable content), it jumps to the new bottom after the content
213	// is replaced; otherwise the user's scroll position is left untouched.
214	//
215	// reviewTUIModel uses value receivers throughout (matching the Bubble Tea
216	// idiom of returning an updated tea.Model from Update); the viewport is
217	// mutated in place on the returned copy and the caller assigns the result
218	// back.
219	func (m reviewTUIModel) refreshDetailContent() reviewTUIModel {
220		if len(m.rows) == 0 || m.detailIdx < 0 || m.detailIdx >= len(m.rows) {
221			m.detail.SetContent("")
222			return m
223		}
224		wasAtBottom := m.detail.AtBottom()
225		lines := buildEventLines(m.rows[m.detailIdx].buffer, m.detailViewportWidth())
226		m.detail.SetContentLines(lines)
227		if wasAtBottom {
228			m.detail.GotoBottom()
229		}
230		return m
231	}
232	
233	// handleAgentEvent processes an agentEventMsg, updating the relevant row.
234	func (m reviewTUIModel) handleAgentEvent(msg agentEventMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
235		idx, ok := m.rowIdx[msg.agent]
236		if !ok {
237			return m, nil
238		}
239		row := &m.rows[idx]
240	
241		// Stamp run-start on the first event from this agent (per-row, not
242		// TUI-start; prevents inflated durations for late-starting agents).
243		if row.runStart.IsZero() {
244			row.runStart = time.Now()
245		}
246	
247		row.buffer = append(row.buffer, msg.ev)
248	
249		switch e := msg.ev.(type) {
250		case reviewtypes.Started:
251			// runStart already set; no other state update needed.
252		case reviewtypes.AssistantText:
253			collapsed := stringutil.CollapseWhitespace(sanitizeDisplayText(e.Text))
254			row.preview = truncateDisplayWidth(collapsed, 80)
255		case reviewtypes.Tokens:
256			row.tokens = e // cumulative: overwrite, not sum
257		case reviewtypes.Finished:
258			// RunError is sticky: if a prior RunError event already classified
259			// this row as Failed, a subsequent Finished{Success: true} must NOT
260			// flip it back to Succeeded. CU3's parser-fix-loop guarantees that
261			// RunError + Finished{Success:false} both accompany torn streams;
262			// matching that contract here keeps the TUI consistent with
263			// classifyStatus from CU4 (which honors sawRunError).
264			if row.status != reviewtypes.AgentStatusFailed {
265				if e.Success {
266					row.status = reviewtypes.AgentStatusSucceeded
267				} else {
268					row.status = reviewtypes.AgentStatusFailed
269				}
270			}
271			row.runEnd = time.Now()
272		case reviewtypes.RunError:
273			row.status = reviewtypes.AgentStatusFailed
274			row.err = e.Err
275			if row.runEnd.IsZero() {
276				row.runEnd = time.Now()
277			}
278		case reviewtypes.ToolCall:
279			// No visible state update for tool calls in the dashboard.
280		}
281	
282		// Re-render the focused agent's viewport content when a new event lands
283		// for it. refreshDetailContent's AtBottom check preserves user scroll if
284		// they've scrolled up; auto-tails otherwise.
285		if m.detailMode && m.detailIdx == idx {
286			m = m.refreshDetailContent()
287		}
288	
289		return m, nil
290	}
291	
292	// handleKey processes keyboard input.
293	func (m reviewTUIModel) handleKey(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
294		// Post-finish dashboard: only explicit exit keys dismiss. Any other key
295		// (including Ctrl+O) falls through to normal handling so the user can
296		// still drill into completed agent output. Ctrl+C also quits immediately
297		// — there are no agents left to drain.
298		if m.finished && !m.detailMode {
299			if isPostFinishExitKey(msg) || (msg.Code == 'c' && msg.Mod == tea.ModCtrl) {
300				return m, tea.Quit
301			}
302		}
303	
304		switch {
305		case msg.Code == 'c' && msg.Mod == tea.ModCtrl:
306			if m.detailMode {
307				// In drill-in: Ctrl+C is intentionally ignored; Esc first.
308				return m, nil
309			}
310			// Second Ctrl+C while a cancellation is already in flight force-quits
311			// without waiting for agents to drain. The shared CancelFunc is
312			// guarded by cancelOnce, so the second press doesn't double-cancel.
313			if m.cancelling {
314				return m, tea.Quit
315			}
316			m.cancelling = true
317			m.cancelOnce.Do(m.cancel)
318			// Do NOT quit on the first Ctrl+C: leave the TUI up so the user sees
319			// the cancelling indicator while agents drain. Natural finish
320			// (runFinishedMsg) or a second Ctrl+C dismisses the TUI.
321			return m, nil
322	
323		case msg.Code == 'o' && msg.Mod == tea.ModCtrl:
324			if m.detailMode {
325				m.detailMode = false
326				return m, nil
327			}
328			m.detailMode = true
329			if len(m.rows) > 0 && (m.detailIdx < 0 || m.detailIdx >= len(m.rows)) {
330				m.detailIdx = 0
331			}
332			// Resize viewport in case termWidth/termHeight have changed since
333			// last detail-mode entry, then load the focused agent's events and
334			// tail to the bottom.
335			m.detail.SetWidth(m.detailViewportWidth())
336			m.detail.SetHeight(m.detailViewportHeight())
337			m = m.refreshDetailContent()
338			m.detail.GotoBottom()
339			return m, nil
340	
341		case msg.Code == tea.KeyEscape || msg.Code == tea.KeyEsc:
342			if m.detailMode {
343				m.detailMode = false
344				return m, nil
345			}
346			return m, nil
347	
348		case msg.Code == tea.KeyLeft:
349			if m.detailMode && len(m.rows) > 0 {
350				m.detailIdx = (m.detailIdx - 1 + len(m.rows)) % len(m.rows)
351				m = m.refreshDetailContent()
352				m.detail.GotoBottom()
353			}
354			return m, nil
355	
356		case msg.Code == tea.KeyRight:
357			if m.detailMode && len(m.rows) > 0 {
358				m.detailIdx = (m.detailIdx + 1) % len(m.rows)
359				m = m.refreshDetailContent()
360				m.detail.GotoBottom()
361			}
362			return m, nil
363		}
364	
365		// Delegate any unhandled key to the viewport so PgUp/PgDn/Home/End/↑/↓
366		// reach its internal keymap. Only meaningful in detail mode — on the
367		// dashboard the viewport is inert.
368		if m.detailMode {
369			var cmd tea.Cmd
370			m.detail, cmd = m.detail.Update(msg)
371			return m, cmd
372		}
373		return m, nil
374	}
375	
376	// isPostFinishExitKey reports whether msg is one of the explicit exit keys
377	// honored on the post-finish dashboard. Ctrl+C is handled separately in the
378	// normal switch so duplicate-press semantics (cancelling → force-quit) still
379	// apply; here we only need q/Esc/Enter without modifiers.
380	func isPostFinishExitKey(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) bool {
381		if msg.Mod != 0 {
382			return false
383		}
384		switch msg.Code {
385		case 'q', tea.KeyEnter, tea.KeyEscape:
386			return true
387		}
388		return false
389	}
390	
391	// View renders the current state.
392	func (m reviewTUIModel) View() tea.View {
393		var content string
394		if m.detailMode && len(m.rows) > 0 {
395			content = detailFrame(m.rows[m.detailIdx], m.detail.View(), m.termWidth, m.termHeight)
396		} else {
397			content = m.dashboardView()
398		}
399		v := tea.NewView(content)
400		v.AltScreen = m.detailMode
401		return v
402	}
403	
404	// dashboardView renders the summary table.
405	func (m reviewTUIModel) dashboardView() string {
406		var b strings.Builder
407	
408		m.writeDashboardLine(&b, m.headerLine())
409	
410		for _, row := range m.rows {
411			m.writeDashboardLine(&b, m.renderRow(row))
412		}
413		b.WriteString("\n")
414	
415		switch {
416		case m.finished:
417			m.writeDashboardLine(&b, m.countsLine())
418			m.writeDashboardLine(&b, "Ctrl+O: drill in · q/Esc/Enter: exit")
419		case m.cancelling:
420			m.writeDashboardLine(&b, "Cancelling agents... · Ctrl+C again: force quit")
421		default:
422			m.writeDashboardLine(&b, "Ctrl+O: drill in · Ctrl+C: cancel")
423		}
424		return b.String()
425	}
426	
427	func (m reviewTUIModel) writeDashboardLine(b *strings.Builder, line string) {
428		b.WriteString(truncateDisplayWidth(line, m.dashboardWidth()))
429		b.WriteString("\n")
430	}
431	
432	func (m reviewTUIModel) dashboardWidth() int {
433		if m.termWidth <= 0 {
434			return 80
435		}
436		return m.termWidth
437	}
438	
439	// headerLine returns the column header row.
440	func (m reviewTUIModel) headerLine() string {
441		return m.renderTableLine("AGENT", "STATUS", "DURATION", "TOKENS", "PREVIEW")
442	}
443	
444	// renderRow renders one agent row.
445	func (m reviewTUIModel) renderRow(row agentRow) string {
446		name := row.name
447	
448		var statusStr string
449		switch row.status {
450		case reviewtypes.AgentStatusSucceeded:
451			statusStr = "✓ done"
452		case reviewtypes.AgentStatusFailed:
453			statusStr = "✗ failed"
454		case reviewtypes.AgentStatusCancelled:
455			statusStr = "— cancel"
456		case reviewtypes.AgentStatusUnknown:
457			switch {
458			case m.cancelling:
459				// In-flight cancellation: distinct from the terminal Cancelled
460				// state ("— cancel") so the user can see that the cancel signal
461				// has been sent but the agent is still draining.
462				statusStr = "cancelling"
463			case row.runStart.IsZero():
464				statusStr = "queued"
465			default:
466				statusStr = m.spinner.View() + " running"
467			}
468		}
469	
470		durStr := ""
471		if !row.runStart.IsZero() {
472			if !row.runEnd.IsZero() {
473				durStr = formatDuration(row.runEnd.Sub(row.runStart))
474			} else {
475				durStr = formatDuration(time.Since(row.runStart))
476			}
477		}
478	
479		tokStr := ""
480		if row.tokens.In > 0 || row.tokens.Out > 0 {
481			tokStr = fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s", formatCompact(row.tokens.In), formatCompact(row.tokens.Out))
482		}
483	
484		return m.renderTableLine(name, statusStr, durStr, tokStr, row.preview)
485	}
486	
487	func (m reviewTUIModel) renderTableLine(agent, status, duration, tokens, preview string) string {
488		const (
489			agentWidth    = 20
490			statusWidth   = 10
491			durationWidth = 8
492			tokensWidth   = 8
493			minWidth      = agentWidth + statusWidth + durationWidth + tokensWidth + 8 // four two-space separators
494		)
495		termWidth := m.dashboardWidth()
496	
497		previewWidth := termWidth - minWidth
498		if previewWidth < 0 {
499			previewWidth = 0
500		}
501	
502		line := fmt.Sprintf("%s  %s  %s  %s  %s",
503			padDisplayWidth(agent, agentWidth),
504			padDisplayWidth(status, statusWidth),
505			padDisplayWidth(duration, durationWidth),
506			padDisplayWidth(tokens, tokensWidth),
507			truncateDisplayWidth(preview, previewWidth))
508		return truncateDisplayWidth(line, termWidth)
509	}
510	
511	// countsLine produces the summary line shown after the run finishes.
512	func (m reviewTUIModel) countsLine() string {
513		succ, fail, canc := 0, 0, 0
514		for _, r := range m.summary.AgentRuns {
515			switch r.Status {
516			case reviewtypes.AgentStatusSucceeded:
517				succ++
518			case reviewtypes.AgentStatusFailed:
519				fail++
520			case reviewtypes.AgentStatusCancelled:
521				canc++
522			case reviewtypes.AgentStatusUnknown:
523				// not counted
524			}
525		}
526		return fmt.Sprintf("%d agent(s) done — %d succeeded, %d failed, %d cancelled",
527			len(m.summary.AgentRuns), succ, fail, canc)
528	}

530	// formatDuration formats a duration compactly for the table column.
531	func formatDuration(d time.Duration) string {
532		if d < time.Second {
533			return fmt.Sprintf("%dms", d.Milliseconds())
534		}
535		if d < time.Minute {
536			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fs", d.Seconds())
537		}
538		return fmt.Sprintf("%dm%ds", int(d.Minutes()), int(d.Seconds())%60)
539	}

541	// formatCompact formats a token count as e.g. "1.2k" or "450".
542	func formatCompact(n int) string {

545		}

1	// Package review — see env.go for package-level rationale.
2	//
3	// tui_detail.go provides the alt-screen drill-in renderer. The body content is
4	// produced by [eventLines] (one or more wrapped lines per event) and fed into
5	// a bubbles/v2/viewport on [reviewTUIModel]; this file's [detailFrame] is the
6	// pure-function chrome (header + body + footer) that wraps the viewport's
7	// pre-rendered output and pads to exactly termHeight lines so every frame has
8	// the same line count (avoids ghost rows in Bubble Tea's alt-screen diff).
9	package review
10	
11	import (
12		"fmt"
13		"strings"
14	
15		reviewtypes "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/review/types"
16	)
17	
18	// eventLines converts a single Event to one or more display lines for the
19	// detail view, wrapped to maxWidth display cells. AssistantText preserves
20	// embedded '\n' as paragraph breaks; other event types render as a single
21	// sanitized line that wraps only on width overflow.
22	func eventLines(ev reviewtypes.Event, maxWidth int) []string {
23		if maxWidth <= 0 {
24			return nil
25		}
26		var raw string
27		switch e := ev.(type) {
28		case reviewtypes.Started:
29			raw = "[started]"
30		case reviewtypes.AssistantText:
31			// AssistantText is the only event that can contain meaningful
32			// multi-line content; wrapDisplayWidth honors embedded newlines.
33			return wrapDisplayWidth(e.Text, maxWidth)
34		case reviewtypes.ToolCall:
35			raw = fmt.Sprintf("[tool: %s] %s", e.Name, e.Args)
36		case reviewtypes.Tokens:
37			raw = fmt.Sprintf("[tokens in=%d out=%d]", e.In, e.Out)
38		case reviewtypes.Finished:
39			if e.Success {
40				raw = "[finished: success]"
41			} else {
42				raw = "[finished: failed]"
43			}
44		case reviewtypes.RunError:
45			if e.Err != nil {
46				raw = fmt.Sprintf("[error: %v]", e.Err)
47			} else {
48				raw = "[error]"
49			}
50		default:
51			raw = "[unknown event]"
52		}
53	
54		return wrapDisplayWidth(raw, maxWidth)
55	}
56	
57	// buildEventLines returns every wrapped body line for the supplied event
58	// buffer, in order. The result is suitable for feeding into a viewport via
59	// SetContent.
60	func buildEventLines(buffer []reviewtypes.Event, maxWidth int) []string {
61		if len(buffer) == 0 || maxWidth <= 0 {
62			return nil
63		}
64		out := make([]string, 0, len(buffer))
65		for _, ev := range buffer {
66			out = append(out, eventLines(ev, maxWidth)...)
67		}
68		return out
69	}
70	
71	// detailFrame renders the alt-screen drill-in chrome around a body string. The
72	// body is the viewport's already-rendered view (already clipped to bodyHeight
73	// lines by the viewport itself). detailFrame adds:
74	//
75	//  1. Header line: "─── <name> (<n> events) ─────────────" (filled to termWidth)
76	//  2. Body: trimmed/padded to exactly bodyHeight lines, each padded to termWidth.
77	//  3. Footer line: "←/→ switch agent · Esc back · PgUp/PgDn scroll"
78	//
79	// CRITICAL: the rendered string is exactly termHeight lines. Bubble Tea's
80	// alt-screen diff leaves ghost rows if the line count varies between frames.
81	func detailFrame(row agentRow, body string, termWidth, termHeight int) string {
82		if termWidth < 1 {
83			termWidth = 80
84		}
85		if termHeight < 3 {
86			termHeight = 3
87		}
88	
89		bodyHeight := termHeight - 2
90		if bodyHeight < 0 {
91			bodyHeight = 0
92		}
93	
94		headerContent := fmt.Sprintf("─── %s (%d events) ", sanitizeDisplayText(row.name), len(row.buffer))
95		header := padDisplayWidthWith(headerContent, termWidth, "─")
96	
97		// Normalize the viewport body to exactly bodyHeight lines, each padded to
98		// termWidth so frame width is stable.
99		bodyLines := splitBodyToHeight(body, bodyHeight, termWidth)
100	
101		footerText := "←/→ switch agent · Esc back · PgUp/PgDn scroll"
102		footer := padDisplayWidth(footerText, termWidth)
103	
104		var b strings.Builder
105		b.WriteString(header)
106		b.WriteString("\n")
107		for _, line := range bodyLines {
108			b.WriteString(line)
109			b.WriteString("\n")
110		}
111		b.WriteString(footer)
112		return b.String()
113	}
114	
115	// splitBodyToHeight normalizes a multi-line body string to exactly bodyHeight
116	// lines, each truncated and padded to termWidth. Lines beyond bodyHeight are
117	// dropped; missing lines are padded with spaces.
118	func splitBodyToHeight(body string, bodyHeight, termWidth int) []string {
119		if bodyHeight <= 0 {
120			return nil
121		}
122		var raw []string
123		if body != "" {
124			raw = strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(body, "\n"), "\n")
125		}
126		lines := make([]string, 0, bodyHeight)
127		for i := range bodyHeight {
128			if i < len(raw) {
129				lines = append(lines, padDisplayWidth(raw[i], termWidth))
130			} else {
131				lines = append(lines, strings.Repeat(" ", termWidth))
132			}
133		}
134		return lines
135	}

content.text:
I have everything needed. The tests themselves confirm the `bubbles/v2/viewport` API surface (`Width`, `Height`, `AtBottom`, `GotoBottom`, `GotoTop`, `YOffset`, `TotalLineCount`, `SetContent`, `SetContentLines`, `SetWidth`, `SetHeight`, `View`, `Update`) — if they compile and pass, the API is correct.

Here is the consolidated review across the four lenses you invoked.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The committed change is a textbook *replace-hand-rolled-with-widget* refactor: the old `detailScroll` + `buildBodyLines` + `maxDetailScroll` + `clampScroll` machinery all collapses into `viewport.Model`'s own state, with `refreshDetailContent` as the single adapter that keeps content + auto-tail in sync. Switching a custom scroll calculator to a vetted widget is almost always a quality win in TUI code — fewer index-arithmetic bugs and PgUp/Home/End come "for free".
- The wrap design is interesting: the **viewport receives pre-wrapped lines** via `SetContentLines(buildEventLines(buffer, width))`. That side-steps the viewport's internal soft-wrap (which doesn't know about ANSI display width) and lets `ansi.Wrap` + `sanitizeDisplayText` do width-correct wrapping. The trade-off is that every event arrival re-wraps the whole buffer — see perf note below.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

---

## Scope

- Branch: `feat/review-detail-viewport`
- Commits unique vs `main`: **1** (`a9210fb9f`)
- Files touched: `tui_text.go` (+25), `tui_detail.go` (±~250), `tui_model.go` (±~290), and their tests
- Staged but not yet committed on top: a **separate** "Ctrl+C double-press / explicit post-finish exit keys" feature in `tui_model.go`/`tui_model_test.go`/`tui_sink_test.go`. I treated this as **out of scope** per your "only the commits unique to this branch vs main" instruction; flagging only so you know it's there. (You may want to land the viewport refactor first, then PR the cancellation work separately — those are independent concerns and the PR-review-toolkit's `feedback_few_commits_per_pr.md` memory points the same way.)

## Overview

The drill-in alt-screen (`Ctrl+O`) previously rendered each event as a single truncated line, with manual `detailScroll` math choosing the visible window. This commit:

1. Adds `wrapDisplayWidth` in `tui_text.go` — paragraph-aware (\n is a break), per-paragraph sanitize, ANSI-width-correct wrap via `ansi.Wrap`.
2. Replaces `eventLine` (string) with `eventLines` (`[]string`), and adds `buildEventLines` for the whole buffer.
3. Replaces `detailView` (renders body itself) with `detailFrame` (wraps an already-rendered viewport body in chrome).
4. Adds a `viewport.Model` field on `reviewTUIModel`, seeded with 80×22 defaults so a `Ctrl+O` before any `WindowSizeMsg` doesn't panic.
5. Delegates unhandled keys in detail mode to `viewport.Update`, so PgUp/PgDn/Home/End/mouse wheel work.
6. Preserves auto-tail via `AtBottom()` sampling around `SetContentLines`.

## Code quality and style — strengths

- **Correctness of the wrap behavior is well-pinned.** `TestDetailFrame_WrapsLongAssistantText` (load-bearing) verifies multi-line wrap, `TestDetailFrame_PreservesAssistantTextNewlines` pins paragraph survival, `TestDetailFrame_LinesFitTerminalWidth` and `TestDetailFrame_MultibyteRuneSafe` cover the display-width invariant. This is the right test shape.
- **Comments are load-bearing, not noise.** The CRITICAL note about Bubble Tea's alt-screen frame diff, the AssistantText rationale in `eventLines`, the value-receiver/viewport mutation explanation on `refreshDetailContent`, and the AtBottom-driven auto-tail story all describe non-obvious *why*. Matches CLAUDE.md's guidance that comments explain hidden constraints rather than restate code.
- **Test refactor is correct in direction.** Old tests called `detailView` in isolation; the new `renderDetailViaModel` helper drives rendering through the model with `WindowSizeMsg` + events + `Ctrl+O` + `View()`. Since the viewport is now the source of truth for body lines, exercising in isolation would have lied. Good call.
- **Defensive defaults are reasonable.** `newReviewTUIModel` seeds 80×24 (instead of 0×0) so the first frame before `WindowSizeMsg` arrives still renders. Symmetric with the `TestTUIModel_InitializesDetailViewport` invariant.
- **Auto-tail invariant is well-formed.** `wasAtBottom := m.detail.AtBottom()` before `SetContentLines`, then `GotoBottom` only if it was already at bottom. The `TestTUIModel_AutoFollow_PreservesUserScroll` test pins both directions (scrolled-up event = no yank; bottom event = stays at bottom).

## Issues / risks (none of these are blockers)

### 1. Perf: re-wrapping the entire buffer on every event arrival (medium)

`handleAgentEvent` → `refreshDetailContent` → `buildEventLines(buffer, width)` re-wraps every event in the buffer every time a new event arrives for the focused agent. For a long review with thousands of events, this is **O(N²)** total work over the run.

**Suggestion:** if this shows up in practice, cache wrapped lines per event (e.g. a `[][]string` parallel to `buffer`) and only wrap the appended event, plus invalidate on `WindowSizeMsg` (only width changes invalidate the cache). Not worth doing speculatively — only if a real review session feels janky.

### 2. Defensive-default inconsistency between `detailFrame` and `detailViewportHeight` (low / cosmetic)

- `detailFrame`: `termHeight < 3 → 3` (bodyHeight = 1)
- `detailViewportHeight`: `termHeight - 2 < 1 → 1` (bodyHeight = 1)

They land on the same value, but via different floors. The dead branch `if bodyHeight < 0 { bodyHeight = 0 }` in `detailFrame` (`tui_detail.go:90-92`) is now unreachable thanks to the `termHeight < 3` guard above it. Either drop the dead `< 0` clamp, or unify the floors by calling `m.detailViewportHeight()` from `detailFrame`'s caller and passing it in. Minor.

### 3. `detailFrame` defaults to width=80 / `detailViewportHeight` defaults to width=1 when `termWidth < 1` (low)

If `termWidth = 0` between init and the first `WindowSizeMsg` (shouldn't happen since `newReviewTUIModel` seeds 80, but still), the viewport produces 1-wide lines while `detailFrame` chrome is 80-wide. The body ends up with one rune followed by 79 padding spaces per line — wasted but not corrupted. Cosmetic; the easy fix is to make both helpers share one floor (e.g. `defaultTermWidth`).

### 4. Empty `AssistantText` now contributes zero body lines, previously one blank line (low)

`wrapDisplayWidth("", width)` returns `nil`. So an `AssistantText{Text: ""}` event used to take a visible row in detail; now it takes nothing. Probably **more** correct (no point dedicating a row to a blank event), but flagging in case there's downstream UX that counted on every event being a visible row.

### 5. Viewport keymap may intercept letters/keys we expect to fall through (low; verify by trying)

`handleKey` delegates *anything* not matched in its switch to `viewport.Update` when in detail mode. The bubbles viewport's default keymap binds `j/k/u/d/g/G/space/b/f` (vim-style) in addition to PgUp/PgDn/Home/End. Two interactions worth a manual smoke test:

- Typing `q` or `c` (without Ctrl) while in detail mode: the model has no case for these and will hand them to viewport, which is harmless (no-op).
- The **staged** post-finish work in your worktree treats `q/Esc/Enter` as exit keys via `isPostFinishExitKey`, but `m.finished && !m.detailMode` gates them out of detail mode — so in detail mode they still fall through to viewport. Fine, but worth a manual `Ctrl+O` → `q` smoke test before merging the staged work.

### 6. `splitBodyToHeight` does work the viewport may already do (low / cosmetic)

`viewport.View()` should already produce `Height` lines clipped to `Width` cells (the viewport knows its dimensions). The subsequent `splitBodyToHeight` is largely there to pad short last-line content out to `termWidth` (when the viewport doesn't right-pad) and to enforce the exact-`termHeight` contract that the alt-screen frame diff needs. It's correct, but the comment on the function could call out *which* property the viewport doesn't guarantee — that's the load-bearing reason this normalization survives.

## Specific suggestions (smallest first)

1. **`tui_detail.go:50` — collapse the early-return in `eventLines`.** Replace:
   ```go
   case reviewtypes.AssistantText:
       return wrapDisplayWidth(e.Text, maxWidth)
   ```
   with `raw = e.Text` and fall through to the bottom `return wrapDisplayWidth(raw, maxWidth)`. `wrapDisplayWidth` already handles embedded `\n` for every input, so the special-casing is now redundant — the comment justifying it is true but no longer load-bearing. Saves a return path; one less branch to keep aligned if the wrap helper changes.

2. **`tui_detail.go:90-92` — drop the `bodyHeight < 0` clamp.** Unreachable after the `termHeight < 3 → 3` guard.

3. **`tui_model.go` — extract a `refreshAndTail()` helper.** The pattern `m = m.refreshDetailContent(); m.detail.GotoBottom()` recurs in Ctrl+O entry and Left/Right cycling. A one-line helper would dedupe three call sites and make the intent ("switch agent, then jump to tail") read more directly.

4. **`tui_model.go:104-107` — viewport seeded height is `defaultTermHeight-2 = 22`, but model `termHeight` is `24`.** Consistent (header+footer = 2), so this is right. But consider extracting `defaultBodyHeight = defaultTermHeight - 2` as a named const so the relationship is self-documenting.

## Security review

This is a pure TUI rendering change. The relevant attack surface is agent-provided text getting written to the user's terminal.

- **ANSI / control-character injection from agent stdout** — addressed correctly. `sanitizeDisplayText` (used both per-paragraph inside `wrapDisplayWidth` and on event chrome strings) calls `ansi.Strip` and then drops all `unicode.IsControl` runes plus `\r`. The `TestDetailFrame_ANSIStripped` test pins this against the cursor-hide / cursor-show CSI sequences codex emits.
- **Width-based truncation is `ansi.StringWidth`-aware**, not byte-count. Multibyte rune safety is pinned by `TestDetailFrame_MultibyteRuneSafe`.
- **No new I/O, no subprocess invocation, no shell escaping, no env var read/write.** No new dependencies (viewport already in `go.sum`).
- **No data leaving the process.** The whole module is render-only.
- **DoS surface**: A maliciously huge `AssistantText` (say 100MB) would allocate proportional memory in `wrapDisplayWidth`'s `strings.Split` and the resulting `[]string`. Mitigated only by upstream limits on agent output, not here. Probably fine for a CLI tool, but worth noting if you ever take an arbitrary attacker-controlled review feed.

Verdict: **clean.** No security issues introduced.

## Simplify review

Two suggestions above (collapse the AssistantText branch; drop the dead `bodyHeight < 0` clamp). Beyond that, this code is already pretty tight — the refactor *itself* is a simplification (~70 net lines deleted from the body-rendering path despite adding `wrapDisplayWidth` and viewport plumbing).

One judgment call worth flagging: `eventLines` and `buildEventLines` are both exported within the package. If `buildEventLines` is the only caller of `eventLines` outside of tests, you could in-line the loop body, but `eventLines` is unit-test-friendly and the symmetry reads well. I'd keep them.

## Test coverage

Strong. The new tests pin every load-bearing claim in the commit message:

- `TestDetailFrame_WrapsLongAssistantText` (the central promise)
- `TestDetailFrame_PreservesAssistantTextNewlines` (paragraph semantics)
- `TestTUIModel_InitializesDetailViewport` (no-WindowSize-yet safety)
- `TestTUIModel_DelegatesScrollKeysToViewport` (PgDn actually reaches viewport)
- `TestTUIModel_AutoFollow_DetailMode` + `TestTUIModel_AutoFollow_PreservesUserScroll` (both directions)
- `TestDetailFrame_PadsToTermHeight` and `TestDetailFrame_EmptyBuffer_PadsToTermHeight` (ghost-row defense)

Gap I'd consider — none **blocking**, but worth a thought:

- A test for the `eventLines` AssistantText empty-string case (does empty AssistantText still keep the buffer's other events visible? probably yes, since `buildEventLines` appends nothing for it, but worth pinning).
- A test for `splitBodyToHeight` with a body that has **more** lines than `bodyHeight` — confirming overflow lines are dropped. The current test set always feeds bodies that fit, so the truncation branch is exercised implicitly via wrap tests but not directly.

## Next steps you may want to take

- Run `mise run check` (fmt + lint + tests) before pushing. I didn't run it; you'll want to before opening the PR.
- Decide on the staged Ctrl+C/post-finish-exit-keys work: keep it in this PR or split out (per the few-commits-per-PR convention, splitting is the cleaner shape since the two concerns are independent).

## Verdict

**Ship it after the two tiny cleanups (suggestions 1 and 2) if you care to.** The refactor is well-motivated, well-tested, and the security and simplification lenses both come back clean. Net effect on the codebase is positive: less custom scroll math, better readability for multi-paragraph review findings, and PgUp/Home/End/mouse wheel now Just Work.
